name: Ehrwalder Alm
kurzbeschreibung: The Ehrwalder Alm at 1,500 m at the foot of the Zugspitze: modern 8-seater gondola, barrier-free Tirolerhaus, and the gateway to Seebensee and Drachensee.
preis: Berg- und Talfahrt Erwachsene 26,00 €, Kinder (6–15 J.) 16,00 €
oeffnungszeiten: Mitte Mai bis Anfang Nov täglich 08:30–16:30 Uhr (Hochsommer ab 08:00–17:30 Uhr)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Ehrwalder Alm spreads out as a vast, sunny high plateau at around 1,500 metres above sea level at the south-western foot of the mighty Wetterstein mountains in Ehrwald. Nestled between the rock massifs of the Zugspitze (2,962 m) and the Mieminger Chain, this high valley is one of the most popular excursion destinations of the Tyrolean Zugspitz Arena. Whether it is a leisurely family hike around the Almsee, a rest on sunny panorama terraces or a demanding mountain tour to the crystal-clear mountain lakes Seebensee and Drachensee – the Ehrwalder Alm offers nature experiences for every generation.

History & Cable Car

Tourist development began in 1962 with the construction of a first chairlift. In 2001 the facility was fundamentally modernised and replaced by the high-performance 8-seater Ehrwalder Almbahn monocable gondola, which carries guests from the valley station (1,108 m) to the mountain station at 1,502 metres in just about eight minutes. At the end of 2022 the cable car company upgraded the lift with 99 ultra-modern, barrier-free panorama cabins from the company Carvatech. Directly at the mountain station, the multi-award-winning flagship mountain restaurant Tirolerhaus was built in 2012, combining alpine cosiness with contemporary timber architecture. From the Alm the classic hike leads to the Seebenalm and on to the emerald-green Seebensee (1,657 m), in whose mirror-smooth surface the rock faces of the Zugspitze are picturesquely reflected. Higher still, the Coburger Hütte (1,920 m) sits enthroned by the mysterious Drachensee.

Visit & Getting There

The summer season of the Ehrwalder Almbahn typically runs from mid-May to the beginning of November daily from 08:30 to 16:30 (in high summer, July to September, already from 08:00 to 17:30). In winter the ski season runs from mid-December to Easter. Cable car prices Summer 2025/2026: return ticket for adults 26.00 € (single trip 17.00 €), youths (16–18 years) 21.00 €, children (6–15 years) 16.00 €, small children under 6 years ride free; family tickets from 59.50 €. Getting there by public transport: take the Außerfernbahn (ÖBB/DB) to Ehrwald station, from where the regional hiking and guest bus (line 1) runs directly to the Ehrwald Almbahn stop. By car: toll-free from the north via Garmisch-Partenkirchen to Ehrwald or from the south over the Fernpass (B179); large free parking areas are available directly at the valley station (Kroppbühel 10).

Tips

The Ehrwalder Almbahn and the Tirolerhaus mountain restaurant are exemplary in their barrier-free design: the gondolas stop without a step for wheelchair users and prams, and the restaurant offers certified WCs. The circular trail around the Ehrwalder Almsee directly at the mountain station is suitable for prams; free handcarts can be borrowed at the mountain station. (Please note: the alpine trail to the Coburger Hütte is not suitable for prams). On hot high-summer days, start with the first gondola at 08:00 to the Seebensee.
